text:
Maya: Heads-up — sigma-int4 onboarding eval shows a consistent sentence-boundary missegment for Japanese kana-heavy subtitles. BLEU down ~3.8 on the tsukuba-subset. Repro steps below.

Maya: repro command:
```
python -m evals.run --model sigma-int4 --suite subtitles-ja --metric bleu --split sample-1000
```
Output highlights sentence splits that shouldn't be there around small kana and elongated onomatopoeia. Example diff pasted later.

Yuki: Can you paste a tiny failing example? :eyes:

Maya: sure — original / reference / model output (token boundaries annotated):
```
REF: お願いします。
SYS: お願いします。

REF: ぎゅっ……
SYS: ぎゅ
……
```
Model inserts a hard break between small-tsu-ish sequence and ellipses.

EvalBot: failing_samples: 12; top_pattern: "kana-run + punctuation -> split before punctuation"; attached gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/fake-gist-kana-split (sample list).

Siddharth: Is this limited to quantized model (int4) or seen on q8/q5 too?

Maya: FP16 baseline passes on the same suite. q8 shows a tiny delta (~0.3) but int4 spikes. Looks correlated with the tokenizer table used for quantized runtime (we replaced some byte-to-char sentinel handling in q4->q5 kernel).

Eli: My quick read — the SBD (sentence boundary detector) heuristic in tokenizer assumes that punctuation attached to a preceding grapheme cluster remains inside the token. The quantized tokenizer lookup may have pruned zero-width markers causing the grapheme merge to fail.

Anjali: Can you try toggling tokenizer mode to legacy to confirm? `--tokenizer-mode legacy` or `TOKENIZER_LEGACY=1` in env. If legacy fixes it, then it's a tokenizer regression not the LM arithmetic.

Maya: did that: legacy mode reduces failures to 1/12. So definitely a tokenizer/path issue.

Yuki: @Maya can you dump token ids around the split for one failing sample?

Maya: pasted token id window (hex tokens for readability):
```
... 0x12f 0x2a7 0x0 (ZWSP?) 0x3b 0x3c 0xffe (ELLIPSIS) ...
```
In legacy mode the ZWSP-like marker id is present, in quantized tables it becomes 0x0 and gets treated as break.

Siddharth: Could be a side-effect of table compression (we drop low-frequency control tokens to save LUT size). Which commit added compression? @Eli any idea?

Eli: I see a PR: `tokenizer:compact-lut` merged two weeks ago (r/312). It introduced a sparse-index remap for low-rank tokens to reduce int4 memory. Suspect bug in remap for zero-width joins and small-tsu variants.

Anjali: Short mitigation: re-run quant build excluding control tokens from compaction (list: ZWJ U+200D, ZWNJ U+200C, HANGUL FILLER, small tsu variants). I can push a patch to the quant pipeline to preserve those.

Maya: that would be ideal. For now, I added a temporary eval guard that warns when SBD splits increase >1.5x for ja-subtitles on any bring-up. Filed bug: ML-8723.

Yuki: I'll bisect tokenizer PRs between `r/300`..`r/315` tomorrow morning and ping infra to repro on dedicated int4.

Siddharth: Also let's add a small unit test to the tokenizer repo: take a short list of kana-heavy subtitle snippets and assert no sentence splits. If it fails, fail the build. That prevents regressions from slipping through.

Maya: added test draft in my fork: `tests/test_sbd_kana.py` — will open PR once we confirm the compaction patch.

Eli: Quick note — this only affected subtitle-style inputs (short, line-broken, onomatopoeic punctuation). Long-form text unrelated. We should include this in release notes as a targeted fix.

Anjali: On quant pipeline side I'll add a flag `--preserve-control-toks` and run a small smoke matrix across ja/ko/zh. Will update thread when job finishes (~1h). :hourglass_flowing_sand:

EvalBot: scheduled job `quant-preserve-smoke-ja` queued on dedicated-gpu-3; notify: #eng-ml when done.

Maya: Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick triage. I'll attach failing sample set and the BLEU diffs to ML-8723. :thumbsup:

Yuki: ack, thanks — I'll take the bisect and coordinate with Anjali for a candidate hotfix.

(End of thread)
